Dexterity

dek-STER-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Dexterity is skill and grace in physical movement, especially with the hands.

Watching the cardsharp shuffle the deck, the tourists couldn't tell whether to admire his dexterity or worry about their wallets.

Worked Example

The street magician's dexterity made the coin seem to vanish and reappear, his fingers moving faster than the audience could follow.

Dexterity is skillful, graceful physical control, especially fine or delicate movements of the hands.

How Dexterity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

skillfulness

skillfulness: the quality of being skilled at something

adroitness

adroitness: cleverness or skill, especially in physical or mental tasks

Antonyms

clumsiness

clumsiness: a lack of physical grace or skill

awkwardness

awkwardness: a lack of grace or ease in movement

How Strong Is It? — competence → dexterity → virtuosity

competence vs. dexterity

competence vs. dexterity: Competence simply means having enough skill to do a task adequately, without the impressive grace of true dexterity.

virtuosity vs. dexterity

virtuosity vs. dexterity: Virtuosity is an even higher, rarer level of skill than ordinary dexterity, often reserved for masters of an art or craft.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — dexter-

root — dexter-: skillful; right-handed (Latin dexter, 'on the right side')

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Dexterity comes from Latin dexter ('on the right side,' also 'skillful,' since most people are right-handed), the same root behind the everyday word dexterous, plus -ity -- 'the state of being skillful.'

Use the root in a new word: dexterous

Use the root in a new word: dexterous: The chef's dexterous knife work let her dice an entire onion in seconds.
